name: Lucas
title: live panda cams
cardText: Native to central China, giant pandas have come to symbolize vulnerable species.
know: Pandas are often seen eating in a relaxed sitting posture, with their hind legs stretched out before them. They may appear sedentary, but they are skilled tree-climbers and efficient swimmers.
text: Giant pandas are very unusual animals that eat almost exclusively bamboo, which is very low in nutrients. Because of this, they have many unique adaptations for their low-energy lifestyle. Giant pandas are solitary. They have a highly developed sense of smell that males use to avoid each other and to find females for mating in the spring. After a five-month pregnancy, females give birth to a cub or two, though they cannot care for both twins. The blind infants weigh only 5 ounces at birth and cannot crawl until they reach three months of age. They are born white, and develop their much loved coloring later. Habitat loss is the primary threat to this species. Its popularity around the world has helped the giant panda become the focus of successful conservation programs.
donationText: Our process for bamboo donations first starts with a site evaluation. It is important that our team sees where the bamboo is growing, then determining if the bamboo is a species that our animals are currently eating. Thank you for your interest in donating bamboo for our pandas.

name: Sam & Lora
title: Bald Eagle cams
size: Body: 34 to 43 inches; wingspan: 6 to 8 feet
habitat: Seacoasts, rivers, large lakes or marshes
cardText: Pair of eagle parents lay and protect eggs, feed their chicks and teach them to hunt and fly.
know: Because of its role as a symbol of the US, but also because of its being a large predator, the bald eagle has many representations in popular culture. Not all of these representations are accurate. In particular, the movie or television bald eagle typically has a bold, powerful cry. The actual eagle has a much softer, chirpy voice, not in keeping with its popular image.
text: The bald eagle, with its snowy-feathered (not bald) head and white tail, is the proud national bird symbol of the United States—yet the bird was nearly wiped out there. For many decades, bald eagles were hunted for sport and for the "protection" of fishing grounds.  These powerful birds of prey use their talons to fish, but they get many of their meals by scavenging carrion or stealing the kills of other animals. They live near water and favor coasts and lakes where fish are plentiful, though they will also snare and eat small mammals. Bald eagles are believed to mate for life. A pair constructs an enormous stick nest—one of the bird-world's biggest—high above the ground and tends to a pair of eggs each year. Immature eagles are dark, and until they are about five years old, they lack the distinctive white markings that make their parents so easy to identify.
donationTitle: Keep the Bald Eagle cams Streaming!
donationText: Watch as this lifelong pair of eagle parents lay and protect eggs, feed their chicks and teach them to hunt and fly. Sam & Lora have stolen the hearts of thousands of viewers! 100% of the donations from this page will be utilized directly for the streaming and operational costs of this project.

name: Andy
title: lemurs cams
size: Head and body: 17.75 inches; tail: 21.75 inches
cardText: Lemurs are considered the world’s most endangered group of mammals.
know: A ring-tailed lemur mob will gather in open areas of the forest to sunbathe. They sit in what some call a "yoga position" with their bellies toward the sun and their arms and legs stretched out to the sides.
text: Ring-tailed lemurs are named for the 13 alternating black and white bands that adorn their tails. Unlike most other lemurs, ringtails spend 40 percent of their time on the ground, moving quadrupedally along the forest floor. Ring-tailed lemurs live in southwestern Madagascar, in arid, open areas and forests in territories that range from 15 to 57 acres (0.06 to 0.2 square kilometers) in size. As with all lemurs, olfactory communication is important for ringtails. Ring-tailed lemurs have scent glands on their wrists and chests that they use to mark their foraging routes. Ringtails eat leaves, flowers and insects. They can also eat fruit, herbs and small vertebrates. Females usually give birth to their first baby when they are three years old, and usually once a year every year after that. All adult females participate in raising the offspring of the group. The median life expectancy for a ring-tailed lemur is about 16 years.
donationTitle: Provide Andy the lemur with fruits!
donationText: More than 90% of lemur species are endangered and might face extinction in the nearest future. Watch the ring-tailed lemurs play and climb in this soothing setting and support them by donating for the fruits they adore.

name: Liz
title: koala cams
size: Length, two to three feet; weight, 9 to 33 pounds
cardText: The elevated walkways bring you to eye level with the koalas as they perch in their forest.
know: Koalas are often called bears, but they are actually marsupials. They carry their babies, called joeys, in a pouch. Koalas sleep up to 18–20 hours a day to conserve energy because eucalyptus leaves provide very little nutrition.
text: Koalas live in eucalyptus forests across eastern Australia. They spend most of their lives in trees, where they eat and sleep. Their strong limbs and sharp claws help them climb and grip branches securely. Koalas feed almost exclusively on eucalyptus leaves, which are tough and low in nutrients. To digest this food, they have a specialized digestive system and a very slow metabolism. Because their diet provides little energy, koalas sleep for most of the day. Female koalas give birth to a tiny, underdeveloped joey that continues to grow inside the mother's pouch for about six months. Although koalas may look calm and cuddly, they are wild animals and play an important role in maintaining the health of their forest ecosystems.
donationText: Koalas are facing immense threats from habitat loss and climate change. Your generous donation will help protect and restore their habitats, support rehabilitation programs, and ensure that these adorable marsupials have a safe future in the wild.

name: Glen
title: gorillas cams
size: Standing height, four to six feet
cardText: Variety of snacks very important for the healthy life of gorillas and his plenty of babies.
know: In addition to having distinctive fingerprints like humans do, gorillas also have unique nose prints. Gorillas are the largest of the great apes, but the western lowland gorilla is the smallest of the subspecies.
text: Western lowland gorillas are the smallest of the four subspecies. They live in thick tropical rainforests, where they find plenty of food for their vegetarian diet. They eat roots, shoots, fruit, wild celery, and tree bark and pulp. Gorillas can climb trees, but they’re usually found on the ground in communities—known as troops. Troops are led by one dominant, older adult male, often called a silverback because of the swath of silver hair that adorns his otherwise dark fur. Troops also include several other young males, some females, and their offspring. The leader organizes troop activities, such as eating, nesting in leaves, and moving about the group's home range. Gorillas prefer traveling on all fours, pushing themselves forward with their knuckles and soles of their feet. Female gorillas give birth to one infant after a pregnancy of nearly nine months. These infants ride on their mothers’ backs from the age of four months through the first two or three years of their lives.
donationTitle: make a difference for the gorillas!
donationText: It is our goal to ensure the conservation and restoration of the gorilla population and their habitat in Central Africa. To do this, we need your help! Bring your food charity straight to Glen and his family.

name: Shake
title: live lion cams
size: Length, six to eight feet (excluding tail); weight, 260 to 550 pounds
cardText: Lions roam the savannas and grasslands of Africa, hunting and raising cubs in the pride.
know: Lions are the only big cats that live in social groups called prides. A pride usually consists of several related females, their cubs, and a small number of adult males. Male lions are known for their impressive manes, which make them look larger and help protect their necks during fights.
text: African lions are powerful predators that live in open savannas and grasslands across sub-Saharan Africa. Unlike most other big cats, lions are highly social animals and live in groups known as prides. Female lions do most of the hunting, working together to catch prey such as antelope, zebras, and wildebeest. Male lions defend the pride’s territory from rivals and other predators. Lions spend much of the day resting to conserve energy for hunting, which often takes place at night. Cubs are born after a gestation period of about three and a half months and are cared for collectively by the females in the pride. Although lions are strong and adaptable, their populations have declined due to habitat loss and conflicts with humans.
donationTitle: Help Protect the King of the Jungle!
donationText: Lions are an iconic species, but their populations are declining due to habitat loss and poaching. By donating, you’ll directly support the protection of lions in the wild, help provide food, and ensure their survival for future generations.

name: Mike
title: Chinese alligator cams
size: Length, five to seven feet; weight, up to 100 pounds
habitat: Freshwater wetlands, rivers, lakes, and marshes
cardText: From nose to tail, belly to back, hard scales protect this petite alligator.
know: The Chinese alligator is one of only two living alligator species in the world. Unlike its larger American relative, it is much smaller and is considered critically endangered. Chinese alligators are known for digging burrows to survive cold winters.
text: Chinese alligators are among the smallest crocodilians in the world. They inhabit slow-moving freshwater rivers, ponds, and wetlands in eastern China. Unlike many reptiles, they are well adapted to cooler climates and spend the winter months in deep burrows they dig into riverbanks. These burrows help protect them from freezing temperatures. Chinese alligators are primarily nocturnal hunters, feeding on fish, snails, crustaceans, and small mammals. Although once widespread, their population has dramatically declined due to habitat loss and agricultural development. Conservation programs are currently working to protect their remaining habitats and support captive breeding efforts to prevent extinction.
donationText: Alligators are essential to the ecosystem, but their habitats are under threat. With your support, we can protect these ancient reptiles, restore their habitats, and ensure the balance of wetlands remains intact for future generations.

name: Senja
title: live tiger cams
size: Length, seven to eight feet (including tail); weight, 165 to 310 pounds
habitat: Tropical forests, peat swamps, and mountainous regions
cardText: Sumatran Tigers are the smallest of the five sub-species, and are found in Indonesia.
know: The Sumatran tiger is the smallest surviving tiger subspecies. Its dark orange coat with closely spaced black stripes helps it blend into dense forests. Sumatran tigers are critically endangered due to habitat loss and poaching.
text: Sumatran tigers live exclusively on the Indonesian island of Sumatra. They inhabit dense tropical forests, where their striped coats provide excellent camouflage. Unlike lions, tigers are solitary animals and prefer to hunt alone. They prey on deer, wild boar, and other medium-sized mammals. Strong swimmers, tigers are comfortable in water and often cool off in rivers and lakes. Female tigers give birth to two to four cubs after a gestation period of about three and a half months. Cubs stay with their mother for up to two years while learning essential hunting skills. Today, conservation programs are working to protect the remaining forests and prevent illegal hunting to ensure the survival of this rare subspecies.
donationText: Tigers are critically endangered, with fewer than 3,500 left in the wild. Your donation will contribute to anti-poaching efforts, habitat preservation, and the care of tigers in sanctuaries. Help us give these magnificent creatures the protection they deserve.
